title: Need help making a dwarf fortress that is built into a mountain [mz]

posts.author: spades141
posts.body: rpg maker mz....Im trying to build a dwarf fortress and i cant figure out the best way of doing it. i mostly use default tileset but would be open to using something other then default if anyone has any ideas. Im gonna have my party have to explore a old abandon dwarf fortress so the town folks have somewhere safe to run to if they need to. but im not good at designing. first game for my kids about a d&D campaign we ran. if someone could give me a little help i tried to find something online that someone else has made but couldnt find anything. i have a rough copy but it looks bad. i can do the interior. just need an entrance to the fortress that is kinda like a lord of the rings thats in the picture below. any tips or even if someone has time to give me a rough draft i could use it would be greatly appicated. im sorry if i ask alot of stuff in the forums. im new and doing my best to make this game for the kiddos. lol.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body: Well, on a technical level, it's really just a cliff wall and a stone wall. The thing is with your default assets it's just gonna look very blocky and way less intricately detailed. I'm not aware of any tilesets that would emulate this look, but getting the idea onto the map is fairly simple, as I said.

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
As SGHarlekin said, you can emulate something similar just by using ruin/castle tiles and smush them into a wall, here is what a random all RTP try could deliver (used some of the dungeon interior as is for the pillars).
Now one could make this prettier by colorgrading the default tiles and do some edits or search for one of the many free tilesets out there for something with more options and/or look for a prettier cliff tile... but per se, this works in a pinch. Since this was a quick sample map I now notice I have some errors in the cliff on the left, but yeah, nothing special needed per se.

posts.author: spades141
posts.body: thank you for the info guys. and avery that looks good. it gives me a good starting point and can mess with it as i go. i guess its time to smash some tilesets together and mess with it til i get it to what i like. thank you
